outcome: low Apgar scores at 1 and 5 minutes
cohort: The study included 110 pregnant women attending antenatal OPD and labor room at KIMS&RF, Amalapuram, whose deliveries and subsequent neonatal outcomes were analyzed.
finding: The study found a preterm birth incidence of 27.5% was associated with maternal risk factors such as underweight, unbooked cases, anemia, hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, PPROM, and UTI, leading to poor neonatal outcomes including lower Apgar scores, low birth weight, IUGR, and respiratory morbidity.
